Wellington Management — Technology Undergraduate Summer Internship
Boston, MA (280 Congress)

Re: Technology Undergraduate Summer Internship — Workday Campus **R94778**

I am applying to the 2027 Technology Undergraduate Summer Internship in Boston. I want a ten-week cohort where I design, build, test, and deliver a software application on a real business challenge — software engineering and data analysis next to stakeholders — not TAP, not Business Associate, and not an investment-analyst seat. I am a B.S. Computer Science and Economics student at the University of Michigan (Expected May 2028, GPA 3.66). I am a current junior and a U.S. citizen. I do not need visa sponsorship. I can be in Boston June 2027, 40 hours/week, hybrid 4 days in office / 1 remote.

**Why Wellington.** Wellington is a private-partnership asset manager whose technologists sit on Client, Infrastructure, and Investment platforms and ship software that a global investment organization actually runs. I care about that shape of work: production systems over messy financial and operational data, not a generic web rotation. I have not interned at an asset manager. I would ramp on Wellington's stack and domain with the team rather than pretend I already know the platforms.

**Why this Technology intern (build / test / deliver + data analysis).** What I can defend:

- **Software application + stakeholders.** At Michigan Data Consulting I was the sole engineer on a five-month Michigan Campaign Finance Network contract. I replaced ~2-hour manual committee pulls with a Requests + Pandas ETL (eliminating ~800 hours across 400 tracked PACs) and delivered a production Flask REST API on AWS EC2 into their public research workflow. I scoped ingestion through REST endpoints directly with MCFN — no backend team behind me. That is the closest analog I have to requirements gathering, application design, coding, and iterative delivery with non-engineer users.
- **Data analysis + testing.** I founded Vylet (vyletdata.com), a live PE/search-fund lead-sourcing product at $1,500 MRR across three clients. I turned a ~30-minute manual process into a Dockerized LangGraph pipeline (30 scored leads in 30 minutes — a 30x speedup) with Redis/Celery workers. I engineered a LangSmith eval harness over 20 adversarial cases and 13 archetype labels that lifted extraction faithfulness from 50% to 90% with Pydantic consensus gates, and an asyncpg data layer with injection-safe SQL freshness checks. On SignalWeaver (github.com/Verdent06/SignalWeaver) I served financial-research scores through FastAPI REST (9.1s p50 / 15.2s p99 across 90 tickers) and a GitHub Actions CI pipeline (frontend build, pytest, API image). Research assistant, not investment advice.
- **AM-adjacent data, honestly scoped.** At Lyndbrook Capital I contracted pre-LOI for a boutique search fund: aggregated EPA ECHO and MassGIS data, delivered 800+ Day-1 acquisition targets, and built a Review Velocity scoring algorithm that cut 800 targets to a 280-lead shortlist (35% precision against the fund's revenue criteria). That is messy public data → score → shortlist. It is not Wellington's Client/Infrastructure/Investment platforms.

**Collaboration / cohort project.** I have not done a Wellington-style intern cohort. Closest stories: sole-engineer delivery with MCFN researchers inside a fixed window, and a live product with paying clients where I owned a workstream end-to-end. I would take ownership of a workstream, partner with teammates, and present outcomes to senior leaders at the end of the summer.

**AI-tool curiosity (real work, not Copilot).** I am curious about emerging technologies the same way the JD asks: I already use them in shipped systems. Vylet is a Dockerized LangGraph pipeline with a LangSmith eval loop and Gemini embeddings behind injection-safe SQL. SignalWeaver serves composite scores through FastAPI. I have not used Snowflake, Databricks, Copilot, Fusion, Tableau, or Kubernetes, and I will not check those boxes.

I can be in Boston for the full 10-week program beginning June 2027. I return to Michigan afterward (Expected May 2028).

Vedant Desai
